headline: High-risk filesystem/MCP interaction from Continue into a non-runnable course artifact is unlikely to be harmful, but prompt-injection and data-leakage pathways exist if the course content is treated as input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so if it ingests content from the zoomcamp materials or copied prompts, malicious instructions could steer tool use. The zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and has no direct I/O, so the risk is indirect, but Continue’s filesystem/MCP surfaces make the pathway plausible.
conditions: IF Continue is configured to read course files or pasted text as instructions
IF an MCP server exposes actions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP servers not needed for the session
Keep course materials in a read-only folder
Require explicit confirmation before tool calls
Separate instruction prompts from downloaded course content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for MCP/file inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write/read workspace files, so sensitive code could be exposed if the zoomcamp content is co-located in the same workspace. The zoomcamp artifact itself has no data classes or network egress, so leakage is limited and mostly depends on shared local files rather than remote transmission.
conditions: IF sensitive source code and course files share the same workspace
IF Continue is allowed to read those files during assistance
mitigations: Move sensitive files to a separate workspace
Use a dedicated non-sensitive project folder
Restrict Continue to selected directories
Review recent file accesses after the session
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has broad filesystem write and subprocess capability, while the zoomcamp profile is not runnable and requests no mutable resources. There is no overlapping write target or shared mutable service in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is weak and mainly limited to local workspace contention if the course files are edited.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp materials are placed in the same writable directory as Continue’s workspace
IF another process edits the same files concurrently
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits in the same directory
Use separate git branches or folders
Close duplicate IDE windows on the same workspace
Lock shared files during edits
requires-engineering: add file-lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or explanations that a user may treat as authoritative, but the zoomcamp profile is a course artifact rather than an action-taking agent. Because B does not execute actions, the cascade is mostly limited to incorrect guidance being copied into notes or code, not downstream autonomous harm.
conditions: IF Continue’s output is copied into course notes or code without review
IF the user treats generated explanations as authoritative
mitigations: Verify generated steps against the course source
Ask Continue for citations or rationale
Manually review any code before use
Limit use to drafting, not execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates before reuse

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: Continue’s profile lists generic source code and open editor buffers, while the zoomcamp profile touches no regulated data classes and is not runnable. With no PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data shown, the pairwise compliance pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the workspace
IF the course artifact is repurposed to process sensitive records
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a separate environment for sensitive projects
Review retention settings for editor logs
